request.summary: Build a support risk command center that helps support leads spot aging, blocked, and SLA-near tickets from seeded data
request.user_outcome: Deliver verified outcome: Build a support risk command center that helps support leads spot aging, blocked, and SLA-near tickets from seeded data
non_goals: Do not expand beyond the stated outcome without approval.

success_metrics.name: Outcome verified
success_metrics.target: The requested outcome is satisfied by fresh evidence.
success_metrics.check: Run the verification gates listed in this contract and read their reports.

constraints.description: Keep the first delivery to the smallest useful slice that proves the outcome.

interfaces.name: Primary deliverable
interfaces.contract: The delivered artifact must expose the requested outcome with a clear verification path.

gates.expected_evidence: Build contract is valid or explicitly not applicable.
Gate registry is valid and required gates are declared.
Pre-build estimate exists, validates, and matches runtime budgets.
Run-date stack choices are checked against current official/source material with evidence.
Runtime state is valid or explicitly not applicable.
Phase order and prior-stage evidence are valid before advancement.
Referenced evidence exists and supports the gate or stage verdict it is used for.
Accepted risks and high-risk ship decisions have approved owner signoff with evidence.
All real forks are closed in debate/OPEN.json and any ADR records include decision, rationale, rejected alternatives, dissent, owner, and index evidence.
The raw user request is refined into an enterprise build brief with outcome, scope, acceptance criteria, routing, specialists, verification, and stop conditions.
The raw goal is upgraded into a concrete enterprise blueprint with users, jobs, artifacts, surfaces, acceptance proof, trust, operations, cuts, and final delivery packet.
Agent roster, SDLC stage gates, role independence, frontend/backend coverage, handoffs, worktree boundaries, and audit trail are planned and checkable.
AI tools, models, agents, MCP/plugin surfaces, data boundaries, approvals, output gates, cost controls, audit logs, and rollback controls are inventoried and approved before ship.

Authorization and tenant-isolation surfaces prove deny-by-default decisions, role/permission coverage, negative access tests, anonymous denial, privilege-escalation prevention, audit logging, and signed local evidence before ship.

Personal, sensitive, regulated, or AI-context data surfaces prove inventory, purpose, minimization, lawful basis, retention, deletion/export paths, redacted logging, encryption, transfers, breach response, DPIA handling, tests, and signed local evidence before ship.

Code-producing and deployable work proves local build, shared dev, staging, beta, production, independent review, QA, adversarial checks, rollback, monitoring, signoff, and retro evidence actually ran before ship.
Project-specific AGENTS/CLAUDE/rules context, context budget, baton, and subagent handoff refs are present and checkable.
Upstream source-router receipts prove source id, immutable pinned ref, extracted pattern, rejected parts, safety checks, artifact refs, verification, and rollback where needed.
Loop workspace files, work-log grammar, signal/doc schemas, and domain-loop schema are present and checkable.
The run mines traces, scouts current GitHub sources, proposes bounded improvements, validates regressions, and captures compounding lessons.
An independent evaluator scores the delivered artifact against the requested outcome with rubric evidence, confidence, bias checks, and no blockers.
QA report proves unit/integration, functional, logic, integration, data integrity, security, and UX/resilience checks with fresh evidence.
Documented shell blocks parse cleanly or are intentionally skipped.
Plan and specification shape pass lint.
Stories, requirements, and tasks trace across plan artifacts.
Product signal has a non-stub PRD or is explicitly not applicable.
User-facing product signal has a dated best-in-class benchmark or is explicitly not applicable.
Product/company completeness is explicit across value loop, surface area, business model, trust, ops, and launch.
Every production layer is owned, evidenced, or consciously deferred with risk ownership.
Architecture layers are acyclic, forbidden dependencies stay unreachable, and configured architecture fitness tools pass.
UI work has a design contract or no UI surface applies.
Frontend builds declare browser payload and Core Web Vitals budgets, and built JS stays within budget when output exists.
UI builds provide fresh replayable real-browser evidence: routes, browser, viewport, command output, screenshots, accessibility, and interactions.
Frontend content accessibility checks pass: images have alt text, inputs have labels, links are descriptive, and buttons have accessible names.
Internationalized frontends avoid hardcoded user-facing strings and locale catalogs keep required keys in sync.
Database migration work provides fresh forward, rollback, verification, lock-risk, and backfill evidence.
Database migrations pass zero-dependency safety checks for rollback, expand-contract rollout, Postgres index locking, and unsafe NOT NULL changes.
Database migrations declare the rollback direction required for up-down-up roundtrip proof, with live DB execution recorded when available.
Error handling and async failure rules pass.
Code-producing work has a reproducible developer environment or no code stack applies.
Configuration access is validated and committed env secrets are absent.
Non-functional requirements are quantified when NFR discipline is present.
Observability anti-patterns are absent or no source files apply.
Performance context has tail-latency budgets and no detected regression.
Security checks pass or tool/context absence is recorded.
Known malicious dependency advisories are absent or lookup skipped loudly.
Dependency inventory/SBOM is valid and non-empty, generated by syft, or missing proof tooling is recorded loudly.
Declared API surfaces have machine-readable contracts.
Schema and migration rules pass or do not apply.
Declared required tools are installed.
Declared required skills have machine-readable breadcrumbs or no skill floor applies.
Runtime systems prove SLOs, DORA targets, incident response, on-call, observability, rollback rehearsal, support handoff, and post-incident learning before ship.
Release notes, handoff, and ship artifacts are present where applicable.
README quickstart is present and runnable, or the project has no README yet.
Run traces, refine logs, summary ledgers, or receipts are mined for recurring systemic patterns and proposal-only lessons.
WALTEUR release version, proof counts, registry count, mirrored docs, and component manifest IDs are machine-readable and checked.
Eight-dimension scoreboard meets target, per-dimension floors, security floor, locked targets, evidence refs, and freshness.

Definition of Done is closed at ship/reflect: no unchecked items, checked items carry typed proof references or existing local evidence files, N/A items carry reasons, placeholders are absent, and the checklist is fresh.
Terminal audit certificate has scores, 13-layer walk, intended-vs-implemented evidence, no blockers, no shortfalls, and fresh reproduced evidence.
